text.p: VALLETTA, Sept 6 (Reuter) The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

THE TIMES - PM cites Malta Drydocks as a reason for eliminating subsidies. Says 10-year experiment to make shipyards viable "failing." The government 10 years ago reached agreement with the dockyard on a programme of subsidies and other changes that included capital investment and an early retirement scheme, but Dr Fenech Adami said on Thursday the experiment showed that subsidies did not make sense in the long term.

- Bank branch staff moved after spate of theft. Stolen money returned by priest. The thefts, amounting to some $20,000, were made from a branch of Mid-Med Bank. The bank has decided to move all the staff for "administrative" reasons, a move which has led to complaints by staff who see the action as an outright blame on everyone.
L-ORIZZONT - Labour leader Alfred Sant explains economic policies to GWU leadership..
IN-NAZZJON - Prime Minister says proposed removal of Value Added Tax by Labour Party would lead to more direct taxation.
- Foreign Minister in Rome meetings. Italy's support for Malta's membership of EU confirmed.
